results.evidence: The route description gives '8 hr round trip from Lake Ann' at the end of its descent paragraph, supporting descent_text and the approach variant rather than an 8-hour descent. The SummitPost route page carries the same text word for word (same write-up, counts once); no independent party's timing was found, and the row splits 2-2. Would settle with: an independent trip report giving either the round-trip or the descent time.

The route description gives only 3,300 ft of face height and no car-to-car gain; no outside source states a total gain for this route, and gain_ft may not be computed from pin arithmetic. Would settle with: a trip report stating car-to-car gain from the Lake Ann trailhead.

results.fact: Route breakdown repeats the icefall/headwall section
results.evidence: Already resolved: the current pitch_detail no longer contains '300 ft through the lower icefall to the headwall base'; it now runs lower snow, ice chimney, upper snow, rock step, glacier tongue, 60-70 degree ice to the headwall, matching the beta and the route description's single approach to the headwall.

Neither the route description (MP and its SummitPost duplicate) nor any other page found names an East Buttress on this line or gives a retreat route; the only related advice is to stay high below the Hourglass in low visibility on the descent to avoid the Upper Curtis icefall. Would settle with: an independent description of the retreat options from the couloir.

results.fact: Distance from the glacier corner to the first large crevasse
results.correct_value: about 600 ft of steep snow to the first transverse crevasse
results.evidence: approach_variants[0].baseFinding and hazards[0] put the large transverse crevasse in the first 100 ft with ~300 ft of ice/snow above it to the headwall, while beta and pitch_detail[0] (183 m) give ~600 ft of snow to the first crevasse. The route description (and its SummitPost duplicate) says 600 ft of steep snow to the first crevasse, with the 100 ft / 300 ft figures belonging to the second crevasse higher up — so baseFinding conflates the two. Only one independent write-up exists and the row splits 2-2, so not patched. Would settle with: a second independent description of the start.

Two different parties climbed the route in August (a guide's 30 Aug 2009 trip via Fisher Chimneys, and a CascadeClimbers trip report dated 8/11/2012 via the NW Rib), so August is clearly within the climbing season, supporting season Jul-Aug. No source was found stating a preferred window, and none supports May-June as the best months, but nothing establishes a replacement 'best' window either. Would settle with: a route description stating the preferred months for this line.

results.fact: Treeline elevation / where the route joins Monitor Ridge
results.correct_value: Treeline near 3,700 ft at Chocolate Falls; joins Monitor Ridge near 7,400 ft
results.evidence: Treeline: the Mount St. Helens Institute route guide leaves the forest about 2 miles in at Chocolate Falls (3,700 ft) and Puget Sound Outdoors emerges from the trees around 3,750 ft — two independent sources against the waypoint note's 4,600 ft. Merge: Puget Sound Outdoors says the winter and summer routes meet on Monitor Ridge at 7,400 ft; Mountain Project says ~7,000 ft; the approach, approach_variants notes, baseFinding and climbing_route[0]/[1] (7,400 ft and ~850 ft more to the rim) all agree on 7,400, so the waypoint note is the single outlier.

results.evidence: The route description says to head up the fall line generally aiming north from the sno-park, i.e. the slopes climbed face south. USGS point elevations sampled along the line from the sno-park to the rim give a downslope direction of 154-168 degrees on the lower and middle route and ~214 degrees near the rim — a south-facing flank, not west. Aspect set to S and the face label made consistent.

dist_km 8 (~5 mi one way) matches the Institute's ~10 mi round trip and the summit pin's 5.4 mi, while Puget Sound Outdoors says ~5.5 mi one way and WTA and the Forest Service say ~12 mi round trip (the itinerary's figure). Stored value is the same quantity (one-way) and sources genuinely range 5-6 mi, so not patched. Would settle with: a measured GPS track length.
